sets.title: Which bean plant grew?
sets.summary: Students listen to a class talk about two bean plants and answer questions that move from details to explaining why the plants grew differently, using because and so.

script.title: The Bean Plant Test
script.setting: A teacher and a student talk about a plant investigation in class.

lines.speaker: Mr. Diaz
lines.text: Good morning, class. Two weeks ago, we planted 2 bean seeds. We put them in the same kind of cup with the same soil.

lines.speaker: Mr. Diaz
lines.text: First, we put cup A by the sunny window. Next, we put cup B in the dark closet. We gave both cups the same water every day.

lines.speaker: Amara
lines.text: Today cup A has a tall green plant. It has 6 leaves.

lines.speaker: Amara
lines.text: Cup B has a short plant. It is yellow, and it has only 2 leaves.

lines.speaker: Mr. Diaz
lines.text: Good observing, Amara. Why do you think the plants are different?

lines.speaker: Amara
lines.text: I think cup A grew better because it got sunlight. Both plants got water, so water is not the difference.

lines.speaker: Mr. Diaz
lines.text: Yes. Plants need light to make food. Tomorrow, we will move cup B to the window. Then we will watch to see if it turns green.

choices.why: A tree is a plant, but the class did not plant a tree.
choices.misconception: Over-generalizes from the word plant to a different plant

choices.why: The teacher says the class planted 2 bean seeds.
The talk does not say anything about apples.
choices.misconception: Adds information that was not said

items.stem: Where did the class put cup A?

visual.alt: A sun and a small plant

choices.why: The dark closet is where the other cup went.
choices.misconception: Mixes up the two cups

choices.why: The teacher never talks about his desk.
choices.misconception: Adds information that was not said

choices.why: The teacher says cup A went by the sunny window.

items.stem: What was the same for both cups?

choices.why: The teacher says both cups got the same water every day.
The light was the one thing that was different for the cups.
choices.misconception: Confuses the thing that changed with what stayed the same

choices.text: They had the same number of leaves.
choices.why: Listen again to the numbers of leaves; they are not the same.
choices.misconception: Misremembers the numbers that were said

choices.text: They were both in the closet.
choices.why: Only one cup was in the closet.
choices.misconception: Over-generalizes one detail to both cups

items.stem: How is the plant in cup B different from the plant in cup A?

choices.text: It is tall and green, with 6 leaves.
choices.why: This describes the plant in cup A, not cup B.
choices.misconception: Mixes up the two cups

choices.text: It has more leaves than the plant in cup A.
choices.why: Amara says cup B has only 2 leaves, which is fewer.
choices.misconception: Misreads which number is bigger

choices.text: It got no water at all.
choices.why: The teacher says both cups got water every day.
choices.misconception: Adds information that goes against what was said

choices.text: It is short and yellow, with only 2 leaves.
choices.why: Amara says the plant in cup B is short and yellow with only 2 leaves.

items.stem: Why does Amara say water is NOT the reason the plants are different?

choices.text: Plants do not need water to grow.
choices.why: Plants do need water; Amara does not say they do not.
choices.misconception: Over-generalizes into a false rule

choices.text: Both plants got the same water, so only the light was different.
choices.why: Amara says both plants got water, so water cannot explain the difference.

choices.text: Cup B got more water than cup A.
choices.why: The talk says the cups got the same water.
choices.misconception: Adds information that was not said

choices.text: The teacher forgot to water cup B.
choices.why: Nobody says that cup B was not watered.
choices.misconception: Invents a cause that was not said

items.stem: Why will the class move cup B to the window tomorrow?

choices.text: Because cup B needs more water
choices.why: The window gives light, not water.
choices.misconception: Reverses the cause the speakers gave

choices.text: To make cup A grow taller
choices.why: Cup A is already by the window, so moving cup B will not change it.
choices.misconception: Confuses which cup the plan is about

choices.text: To test if light will help it turn green
choices.why: The teacher says they will watch to see if cup B turns green in the light.

choices.text: Because the closet is too cold
choices.why: No one talks about the closet being cold.
choices.misconception: Adds a reason that was not said

sets.title: Our class reading chart
sets.summary: Students listen to a class discussion of a reading chart and answer questions about numbers, comparing words (most, fewest) and adding to find a total and a difference.

script.title: Counting Books We Read
script.setting: A teacher and two students look at a class chart about books read in one week.

lines.speaker: Ms. Kim
lines.text: Let's look at our reading chart. Each group counted the books they read this week.

lines.speaker: Ms. Kim
lines.text: The Red group read 8 books. The Blue group read 5 books. The Green group read 9 books.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The Green group read the most books. 9 is more than 8.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: The Blue group read the fewest. But they read long chapter books.

lines.speaker: Ms. Kim
lines.text: That is a good point, Fatima. Now let's find the total. How many books did all 3 groups read together?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: First, I add 8 and 5. That makes 13. Next, I add 9 more. The total is 22 books.

lines.speaker: Ms. Kim
lines.text: Great adding, Leo. Our goal for next week is 28 books. We can do it if every group reads 2 more books.

items.stem: How many books did the Red group read?

choices.why: The teacher says the Red group read 8 books.
5 is the number for a different group.
choices.misconception: Matches a number to the wrong group

choices.why: 9 is the number for a different group.
choices.misconception: Matches a number to the wrong group

items.stem: Which group read the most books?

choices.why: The Red group read a lot, but one group read 1 more.
choices.misconception: Picks a close number instead of the greatest

choices.why: The Blue group read the fewest books, not the most.
choices.misconception: Confuses most and fewest

choices.why: Leo says the Green group read the most books.

items.stem: What did Fatima say about the Blue group?

choices.why: Fatima talks about the group that read the fewest books.
choices.misconception: Confuses most and fewest

choices.text: They read the fewest books, but the books were long.
choices.why: Fatima says the Blue group read the fewest, but they read long chapter books.
8 is not the number for the Blue group.
choices.misconception: Matches a number to the wrong group

choices.text: They did not like chapter books.
choices.why: Fatima does not say how the group felt about the books.
choices.misconception: Adds information that was not said

items.stem: What did Leo do first to find the total?

choices.why: Leo did add 9, but that was his next step.
choices.misconception: Confuses the order of steps

choices.why: 28 is the goal for next week, not part of Leo's adding.
choices.misconception: Picks a number that was said for a different idea

choices.why: Leo added the numbers; he did not take away.
choices.misconception: Uses the wrong operation

choices.why: Leo says, first, I add 8 and 5.

items.stem: This week the class read 22 books. How many more books does the class need to read to reach next week's goal?

choices.why: 22 is how many books the class read this week.
choices.misconception: Picks a number that was said instead of finding the difference

choices.why: This adds the two numbers, but the question asks how many more.
choices.misconception: Adds when the question asks for a difference

choices.why: The goal is 28 and the class read 22, and 28 take away 22 is 6.
2 is how many more books each group reads, not the whole class.
choices.misconception: Uses a number for one part instead of the whole

items.stem: Why does Ms. Kim say that Fatima made a good point?

choices.text: Reading fewer books can still be a lot of reading if the books are long.
choices.why: Fatima points out that the Blue group read long books, so a small number does not tell the whole story.

choices.text: The Blue group read the most books.
choices.why: The Blue group read the fewest books.
choices.misconception: Confuses most and fewest

choices.text: Short books are better than long books.
choices.why: No one says short books are better.
choices.misconception: Over-generalizes into a rule that was not said

choices.text: Fatima added all the numbers correctly.
choices.why: A different student did the adding.
choices.misconception: Mixes up the speakers

sets.title: Talking about a story
sets.summary: Students listen to a short story and a class talk about it, then answer questions about setting, the order of events, problem and solution, and the lesson, using time words.

script.title: The Lost Kite
script.setting: A teacher reads a short story aloud, and then a student talks about it.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
lines.text: Listen to our story. It is called The Lost Kite.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
lines.text: One windy day, Rosa flew her red kite in the park. Suddenly, the string broke. The kite flew up into a tall tree.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
lines.text: Rosa felt sad. First, she tried to jump, but the tree was too tall. Next, she asked her big brother Tomas for help.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
lines.text: Tomas got a long stick from home. He gently pulled the kite down. At the end, Rosa smiled and said, thank you!

lines.speaker: Sami
lines.text: I think the problem is the kite got stuck. Rosa solved it by asking for help.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
lines.text: Yes, Sami. What lesson does the story teach?

lines.speaker: Sami
lines.text: It teaches that it is okay to ask for help when a problem is too big.

items.stem: Where did Rosa fly her kite?

choices.why: The story does not happen at school.
choices.misconception: Adds a familiar place that was not said

choices.why: Home is where Tomas got something, not where Rosa flew her kite.
choices.misconception: Picks a place word from the story that does not answer

choices.why: The story says Rosa flew her kite in the park.

items.stem: Where did the kite get stuck?

choices.why: The story says the kite flew up into a tall tree.
The kite did not land on a house.
choices.misconception: Picks a place word from the story that does not answer

choices.why: The story does not talk about water.
choices.misconception: Adds information that was not said

items.stem: What did Rosa do first to get her kite back?

choices.why: Rosa did this, but it was her next step.
choices.misconception: Confuses the order of events

choices.why: The story says, first, she tried to jump.
Another character got the stick.
choices.misconception: Gives one character's action to another character

choices.why: The story does not say Rosa bought anything.
choices.misconception: Adds an event that was not said

items.stem: How did Tomas get the kite down?

choices.text: He climbed to the top of the tree.
choices.why: The story does not say Tomas climbed.
choices.misconception: Adds an action that was not said

choices.why: Jumping was something Rosa tried, and it did not work.
choices.misconception: Gives one character's action to another character

choices.text: He waited for the wind to stop.
choices.why: The story talks about wind, but not about waiting for it to stop.
choices.misconception: Builds an answer from a detail that does not answer

choices.text: He pulled it down with a long stick.
choices.why: The story says Tomas got a long stick and gently pulled the kite down.

items.stem: What is the problem in the story, and how is it solved?

choices.text: The string breaks, and Rosa buys a new string.
choices.why: The string does break, but Rosa does not buy a new one.
choices.misconception: Adds a solution that was not said

choices.text: Rosa is sad, and she goes home.
choices.why: Rosa feels sad, but the story does not end with her going home.
choices.misconception: Picks a feeling as the problem and misses the solution

choices.text: The kite gets stuck, and Rosa gets help to bring it down.
choices.why: Sami says the kite got stuck and Rosa solved it by asking for help.

choices.text: The day is windy, and the wind stops.
choices.why: The windy day is the setting, not the problem.
choices.misconception: Confuses setting with problem

items.stem: What lesson does the story teach?

choices.text: It is okay to ask for help with a big problem.
choices.why: Sami says the story teaches that it is okay to ask for help when a problem is too big.

choices.text: Never fly a kite on a windy day.
choices.why: The story never says that flying a kite on a windy day is wrong.
choices.misconception: Turns a detail into a lesson that was not said

choices.why: Tomas helps, but the story does not say brothers are always right.
choices.misconception: Over-generalizes from one character

choices.why: The kite is red, but the story says nothing about which kites fly highest.
choices.misconception: Turns a detail into a lesson that was not said
